title: Preflight checks for Private upgrades (inventory + blocking criteria)
creator: Talia Benson
content:
Context
- Private upgrades have historically failed late (during Helm apply / migrations) due to missing prerequisites: cluster health, storage headroom, artifact availability, auth reachability, etc.
- This ticket is the single source of truth for the v1 precheck inventory: what we check, who owns each check, and whether it must block upgrades or can warn.
- Prechecks run during `redwood-private upgrade plan` and must produce:
  - machine-readable results (for plan gating + audit)
  - human-readable remediation guidance (for operators)

Goals
- Establish a v1 checklist that is safe-by-default.
- Define “must-block” vs “warn” acceptance criteria per check.
- Assign ownership per check (implementation + ongoing maintenance).
- Align the inventory with Change Management policy for Private releases (SRE + Release Eng gates).

Non-goals
- Perfect detection for every customer edge case (we prefer strong, deterministic checks with explicit escape hatches).
- Multi-hop upgrade automation (N-1 -> N is the default supported path in v1).

Definitions (acceptance criteria)
- MUST-BLOCK: the upgrade cannot proceed safely or deterministically; continuing would likely cause downtime, data loss, irrecoverable partial state, or violate support policy. Installer should stop after plan generation, return non-zero, and suggest remediation.
- WARN: upgrade can proceed, but risk is elevated. Installer should require explicit acknowledgement (`--accept-warnings`), and warnings must be included in the plan summary + audit event.
- INFO (optional): informational checks included for operator context (not gating).

Precheck inventory (v1)
Legend: Mode = BLOCK | WARN | INFO. “Owner” is accountable for implementation in the installer and keeping the check current.

1) Connectivity + basic environment
- CHK-001: Kubernetes API reachable + auth works
  - Mode: BLOCK
  - Owner: Rafael Mendes
  - Notes: Validate kubeconfig, can list namespaces, can read required objects; fail fast with actionable error.
- CHK-002: Kubernetes version supported (per Private support matrix)
  - Mode: BLOCK
  - Owner: Quentin Harris
  - Notes: Enforced via compatibility policy; show detected version and supported ranges.
- CHK-003: Cluster time skew / NTP sanity (nodes within threshold)
  - Mode: WARN
  - Owner: Irene Choi
  - Notes: Too much skew can break TLS/OIDC and cause weird rollout failures.

2) Cluster health + scheduling capacity
- CHK-010: Nodes Ready + no widespread pressure conditions
  - Mode: BLOCK
  - Owner: Irene Choi
  - Notes: Block if any control-plane/critical node NotReady or if >X% nodes NotReady.
- CHK-011: Critical namespaces healthy (redwood-system, ingress, cert-manager)
  - Mode: BLOCK
  - Owner: Vanessa Ortiz
  - Notes: Validate Deployments/StatefulSets available; Jobs not failing repeatedly.
- CHK-012: Schedulable capacity for upgrade jobs (CPU/mem headroom)
  - Mode: WARN
  - Owner: Vanessa Ortiz
  - Notes: If cluster is near saturation, pre-upgrade jobs can starve; allow override.

3) Storage + backups readiness
- CHK-020: Persistent volume health + PVCs bound (control plane + DB)
  - Mode: BLOCK
  - Owner: Irene Choi
  - Notes: Catch Pending PVCs, lost PVs.
- CHK-021: Storage headroom for backup + migrations (DB + object store)
  - Mode: BLOCK
  - Owner: Irene Choi
  - Acceptance: Block if <20% free (or <N GiB absolute) on DB volume or backup target; thresholds configurable.
- CHK-022: Snapshot capability available (EBS/CSI) OR logical backup configured
  - Mode: BLOCK
  - Owner: Bruno Silva
  - Notes: Must be able to take a consistent backup before any irreversible step; ensure at least one supported mechanism is configured.
- CHK-023: KMS / encryption configuration present for backups (where required)
  - Mode: WARN
  - Owner: Hanae Suzuki
  - Notes: Warn by default; BLOCK if environment is marked “compliance_required=true” in config.

4) Database + migrations safety
- CHK-030: DB connectivity from installer context + credentials valid
  - Mode: BLOCK
  - Owner: Michael Nguyen
  - Notes: Must verify reachability and auth before plan proceeds.
- CHK-031: DB schema baseline compatible with target version (migration gating)
  - Mode: BLOCK
  - Owner: Michael Nguyen
  - Notes: Uses versioned migration metadata; fail with explicit “manual intervention required” if out-of-band state detected.
- CHK-032: DB lock timeout / long-running transactions risk signal
  - Mode: WARN
  - Owner: Sean Gallagher
  - Notes: Detect long-running queries / locks (best-effort). Warn with recommended quiet period.

5) Auth / RBAC / external dependencies
- CHK-040: Required RBAC permissions available for upgrade
  - Mode: BLOCK
  - Owner: Benji Okafor
  - Notes: Must be able to create Jobs, patch Deployments/StatefulSets, read Secrets/ConfigMaps (scoped to required namespaces).
- CHK-041: OIDC/SAML reachability for admin login (if enabled)
  - Mode: WARN
  - Owner: Victor Alvarez
  - Notes: Debate: do we BLOCK if OIDC unreachable? Current stance: WARN unless upgrade requires re-auth.
- CHK-042: DNS/TLS basics (cluster DNS works, certs not expired for critical endpoints)
  - Mode: WARN
  - Owner: Victor Alvarez
  - Notes: Include cert expiry check for ingress + internal control-plane service certs.

6) Artifacts + versioning
- CHK-050: Target version upgrade path supported (N-1 -> N) per compatibility policy
  - Mode: BLOCK
  - Owner: Quentin Harris
  - Notes: Policy lives in main redwood repo; installer consumes published matrix.
- CHK-051: Artifacts available (charts/images/bundles) and checksums valid
  - Mode: BLOCK
  - Owner: Connor O'Brien
  - Notes: Air-gapped: verify bundle manifest + signatures; online: verify registry/chart availability.
- CHK-052: Current installation is not “dirty” (previous upgrade incomplete)
  - Mode: BLOCK
  - Owner: Rafael Mendes
  - Notes: If prior upgrade state exists and is not finalized, require rollback/cleanup path.

7) Observability + supportability
- CHK-060: Support bundle prerequisites (logs accessible, upgrade state writable)
  - Mode: WARN
  - Owner: Allison Grant
  - Notes: Warn if we cannot persist plan/audit artifacts locally; do not block upgrade for this alone.

Owner commitments
- Each owner must:
  1) implement/maintain the check in the installer framework
  2) provide remediation text with a concrete “next command” or doc pointer
  3) add/maintain automated coverage in the upgrade E2E test suite where feasible (ENG-4877)

UX requirements (CLI)
- Output must group results by severity and category:
  - BLOCKERS (n)
  - WARNINGS (n)
  - INFO (n)
- Each finding must include:
  - stable check id (e.g., CHK-021)
  - short summary
  - detected value(s)
  - expected/threshold
  - remediation steps
  - link to docs (internal path ok for now)

Policy alignment
- SRE + Release Eng require BLOCK checks to pass prior to starting any apply step.
- WARN checks require explicit operator acknowledgement and must be surfaced in the plan artifact and audit log events.

Open questions
- OIDC reachability (CHK-041): should we BLOCK for environments that enforce SSO for all admin access? Proposal: WARN by default; BLOCK if “no breakglass local admin” is configured.
- Storage headroom thresholds (CHK-021): default 20% + absolute minimum; confirm with design partners (on-prem clusters often run tighter).
- DB lock risk (CHK-032): what signals are reliable across Postgres variants and managed offerings?

Definition of Done
- Inventory above reviewed and signed off by:
  - SRE: Sean Gallagher
  - Release Eng: Connor O'Brien
  - Security: Marcus Lin or Hanae Suzuki (backup encryption-related checks)
- For v1 GA:
  - All BLOCK checks implemented in installer and exercised in at least one E2E upgrade test
  - WARN checks implemented OR explicitly deferred with rationale + documented manual checks
  - Precheck results included in upgrade plan artifact and audit events

Latest updates
- 2025-06-04 (Ethan Park): Aligned on three tiers (BLOCK/WARN/INFO) and `--accept-warnings` behavior. Need final call on OIDC reachability.
- 2025-06-11 (Connor O'Brien): Artifact availability + checksum verification will be BLOCK for both online and air-gapped; release gating depends on it.
- 2025-06-17 (Sean Gallagher): Strong preference to BLOCK on any sign of incomplete prior upgrade state (dirty state) to avoid compounding incidents.
comments: 2025-02-10 — Talia Benson: Creating this ticket to consolidate the precheck list + owners. Please add proposed checks here rather than in Slack threads so we can lock acceptance criteria for beta.
2025-02-12 — Irene Choi: Added storage + PVC checks (CHK-020/021). Strong opinion: storage headroom must be a blocker; we’ve seen too many near-misses during snapshot + migration.
2025-03-01 — Victor Alvarez: For DNS/TLS checks, we should keep it WARN unless we can make it deterministic. Cert expiry is deterministic, DNS reachability less so (transient).
2025-03-18 — Michael Nguyen: DB connectivity + schema baseline gating should be BLOCK. If we can’t verify, we shouldn’t start Helm changes at all.
2025-04-05 — Quentin Harris: Compatibility policy needs to be enforced here; I’ll own the supported upgrade path check, but we need a published matrix artifact the installer can consume.

2025-05-09 — Sean Gallagher: Please ensure error messages say whether rollback is possible from that point. Prechecks should run before any irreversible step; otherwise we’re back to manual firefighting.
2025-06-18 — Ethan Park: Marking as In Progress until we close the OIDC/blocking question and confirm thresholds with design partners. Inventory is otherwise stable for beta.
